title: Fixed versus Bayesian adaptive designs for two-arm survival trials
text: Oncology trials require large number patients reach conclusion acceptable error rates. However, data beginning trial already conclusive either direction, one can stop early efficacy futility. faster decision saves time money exposes fewer patients inferior treatment. However, decision thresholds adjusted repeated looks, can cost power. vignette examines Bayesian adaptive design compares fixed log-rank design type error, power, expected events duration, robust hazards proportional.

title: Fixed versus Bayesian adaptive designs for two-arm survival trials
text: simulate trials 400 patients , recruited uniformly 24 months, randomised 1:1, exponential drop-rate 0.005 per month. Event times follow piecewise exponential distribution, .e. hazard piecewise constant; rpwexp() draws inverting cumulative hazard. analysis uses data available calendar time k-th observed event (cut_at_events()). latent data trial simulated , analyses trial data cuts . Interim final analyses therefore use trial, practice. One simulated trial HR = 0.7, cut first interim analysis:

title: Fixed versus Bayesian adaptive designs for two-arm survival trials
text: Schoenfeld’s formula gives number events required HR = 0.7, one-sided type error 2.5 % 80 % power: D = 4 (z_0.975 + z_0.8)^2 / log(0.7)^2, rounds 247. signed log-rank statistic treatment arm z = (O - E) / sqrt(V); reject z < qnorm(0.025) use Cox hazard ratio effect estimate.
code: analyse_fixed(cut$data) #>            z  p_one_sided           hr  #> -2.980246307  0.001440083  0.585602859 run_fixed(trial, n_events = 247) #>      reject          hr       t_cut n_recruited    n_events  #>     1.00000     0.58614    36.43408   400.00000   247.00000

title: Fixed versus Bayesian adaptive designs for two-arm survival trials
text: use exponential working model Gamma(a0, b0) prior per arm, a0 = 1 b0 = 12 / log(2). prior carries information single event, centred control median, negligible compared 124 observed events. conjugate posterior Gamma(a0 + d, b0 + T) per arm, d number events T total exposure time arm. decision quantity posterior probability P(HR < 1 | data); since HR = lambda_t / lambda_c, closed form pbeta(b_t / (b_t + b_c), a_t, a_c), (a_t, b_t) (a_c, b_c) posterior parameters two arms. analyse 124, 185 247 events (50 / 75 / 100 % D), stop efficacy P(HR < 1 | data) > c analysis, stop futility interim analyses P(HR < 1 | data) < 0.2 (non-binding). weak prior, P(HR < 1 | data) close 1 minus one-sided log-rank p-value, numbers show.
code: analyse_bayes(cut$data, a0 = 1, b0 = 12 / log(2)) #>      prob hr_median  #> 0.9986005 0.5856206 1 - analyse_fixed(cut$data)[["p_one_sided"]] #> [1] 0.9985599  run_bayes_adaptive(trial, c_eff = 0.9918, a0 = 1, b0 = 12 / log(2)) #>        reject     stop_look stop_futility            hr      n_events  #>     1.0000000     1.0000000     0.0000000     0.5856029   124.0000000  #>         t_cut   n_recruited  #>    22.7658790   379.0000000

title: Fixed versus Bayesian adaptive designs for two-arm survival trials
text: single analysis, c = 0.975 = 1 - 0.025 essentially reproduce log-rank test. three analyses c = 0.975, simulated type error 4.8 % (normal approximation: 4.9 %). Without futility, design rejects max_k P_k > c, c 97.5 % quantile max_k P_k H0 (calibrate_bayes()). Calibration constant hazards returns c = 0.9873 (theory: 0.9877). 10,000 independent trials, type error 2.37 % (Monte Carlo SE 0.16 percentage points). threshold lies 0.975 (one look) Šidák bound independent looks, 0.9916, every analysis contains data earlier analyses, posterior probabilities three looks positively correlated. calibration run (takes minutes) :
code: set.seed(2026) calibrate_bayes(n_sim = 10000, a0 = 1, b0 = 12 / log(2),                 n = 400, accrual_time = 24,                 rates_c = lambda_c, rates_t = lambda_c,                 dropout_rate = 0.005) #> 0.9873009

title: Fixed versus Bayesian adaptive designs for two-arm survival trials
text: scenarios use control hazard λ = log(2)/12 (median survival 12 months) , hazard changes, single change point 6 months: results precomputed operating_characteristics() (10,000 trials per scenario, see ?oc_results dev/run_oc.R). small run looks like :
code: scenarios <- list(   h0    = list(rates_c = lambda_c, breaks_c = numeric(0),                rates_t = lambda_c, breaks_t = numeric(0)),   ph_07 = list(rates_c = lambda_c, breaks_c = numeric(0),                rates_t = 0.7 * lambda_c, breaks_t = numeric(0)) ) set.seed(3) operating_characteristics(scenarios, n_sim = 50, c_eff = 0.9873,                           a0 = 1, b0 = 12 / log(2)) #>   scenario design reject  reject_se        hr n_events duration n_recruited #> 1       h0  fixed   0.00 0.00000000 1.0036375   247.00 31.08329      400.00 #> 2       h0  bayes   0.02 0.01979899 1.0291276   216.22 27.97236      382.58 #> 3    ph_07  fixed   0.86 0.04907138 0.6894366   247.00 34.97289      400.00 #> 4    ph_07  bayes   0.84 0.05184593 0.6639330   185.40 27.65699      377.44 #>   early_stop stop_futility #> 1       0.00            NA #> 2       0.28          0.26 #> 3       0.00            NA #> 4       0.60          0.00 oc <- oc_results oc$scenario <- factor(oc$scenario,                       levels = c("h0", "h0_break", "ph_07",                                  "delayed", "diminish", "crossing")) oc_null <- oc[oc$scenario %in% c("h0", "h0_break"), ] oc_alt  <- oc[!oc$scenario %in% c("h0", "h0_break"), ]

title: Fixed versus Bayesian adaptive designs for two-arm survival trials
text: Early stop proportion trials stopped interim analysis, efficacy futility. constant calibration, Bayesian design needs quarter fewer events finishes 7 months earlier, cost 5 percentage points power. geometric mean hazard ratio estimates 0.700 fixed design (unbiased) 0.675 adaptive design: trials stop early tend estimate , chance, particularly favourable.
code: ph <- oc[oc$scenario == "ph_07",          c("calibration", "design", "reject", "hr", "n_events",            "duration", "n_recruited", "early_stop")] knitr::kable(ph, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE,              col.names = c("Calibration", "Design", "Power", "HR (geom. mean)",                            "Events", "Duration (months)", "Recruited", "Early stop"))

title: Fixed versus Bayesian adaptive designs for two-arm survival trials
text: Early analyses help effect strongest early (diminish: constant calibration, adaptive design power fixed design) hurt weakest early (delayed, crossing). futility rule stops 4 % trials delayed (real) effect 22 % crossing hazards. crossing hazards, early harm later benefit partly cancel, designs low power.
code: library(ggplot2) ggplot(oc_alt, aes(x = scenario, y = reject, colour = design)) +   geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = reject - 2 * reject_se,                       ymax = reject + 2 * reject_se),                   position = position_dodge(width = 0.4)) +   facet_wrap(~ calibration) +   labs(x = NULL, y = "Power", colour = "Design") +   theme_minimal()

what: Type I error and robustness of the calibration
title: Fixed versus Bayesian adaptive designs for two-arm survival trials
text: log-rank test, nonparametric, keeps level 2.5 % null scenarios. Bayesian design calibrated constant hazards, type error rises 3.2 % arms share hazard change point. exponential working model misspecified, posterior concentrated. Calibrating additionally h0_break gives c = 0.9918, even Šidák bound 0.9916. robust threshold keeps 2.4 % h0_break, conservative (1.8 %) constant hazards costs 6 percentage points power proportional hazards. conclusion simulation-based calibration valid assumptions done .
code: ggplot(oc_null, aes(x = scenario, y = reject, colour = design)) +   geom_hline(yintercept = 0.025, linetype = "dashed") +   geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = reject - 2 * reject_se,                       ymax = reject + 2 * reject_se),                   position = position_dodge(width = 0.4)) +   facet_wrap(~ calibration) +   labs(x = NULL, y = "Type I error", colour = "Design") +   theme_minimal()

title: Fixed versus Bayesian adaptive designs for two-arm survival trials
text: Exponential working model single Gamma prior; piecewise exponential model robust. robust calibration protects null shapes includes. 1:1 randomisation, uniform accrual, interim analyses exact event counts. Crossing hazards: hazard ratio right estimand? (e.g. restricted mean survival time, RMST) maximum number events designs; power recovered larger maximum O’Brien-Fleming-like threshold schedule. scenario single abrupt change hazard ratio, whereas effects typically develop gradually. Smoothly changing hazards, e.g. Weibull distributions, considered; show exponential working model behaves gradual rather abrupt misspecification. rpwexp() can, however, approximate hazards many change points.
